general_information.Description: Description: This course aims to provide students with knowledge related to Interaction and UX, Ui Design in the mobile world including smartphone devices and other wearable devices. In this course, students will be taught the common principles that prevail in mobile interface design in general. Specific guidelines corresponding to three popular mobile platforms such as Android, iOS and Windows will also be discussed. A nimble tool for Interaction and UX research and design, Ui in Mobility will also be introduced and applied through this course. At the end of this course, students will gain practical experience through a project that has phases: research, user segmentation, user persona, userflow, wireframe, Agile Project Management ..., in which they must apply principles have learned. This course will help students perfect the app.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities > - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class > - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose > - Read the textbook in advance > - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment. >

description: Description: This course aims to provide students with knowledge related to Interaction and UX, Ui Design in the mobile world including smartphone devices and other wearable devices. In this course, students will be taught the common principles that prevail in mobile interface design in general. Specific guidelines corresponding to three popular mobile platforms such as Android, iOS and Windows will also be discussed. A nimble tool for Interaction and UX research and design, Ui in Mobility will also be introduced and applied through this course. At the end of this course, students will gain practical experience through a project that has phases: research, user segmentation, user persona, userflow, wireframe, Agile Project Management ..., in which they must apply principles have learned. This course will help students perfect the app.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand key principles of UX, UI, and interaction design in mobile and wearable application development.
Apply design thinking methodologies and user-centered design approaches , together with appropriate research methods to identify, frame and analyze user needs.
Create and improve information architecture, user flows, wireframes and conduct usability testing to refine solutions through an iterative design process.
Implement design systems, visual design, and interactive prototypes through iterative processes, ensuring alignment with target user profiles
Apply AI tools and demonstrate AI literacy to collaborate effectively across UX/UI design stages.
Demonstrate collaboration, communication, and professional working style in design teamwork.

assessments.No Question: Assignment: Project Proposal Overall Task: Students will receive a project brief provided by the instructor or propose their own brief subject to instructor approval. Based on this brief, they will apply Design Thinking (Empathize & Define) and User-Centered Design approaches to explore the problem space. Students will conduct user research, identify and frame user needs, and analyze insights. In addition, they will evaluate the application’s business and technology context. The final assignment will include a research report, user research documentation, technology and business context.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Understand and apply Design Thinking and the principles of User-Centered Design (UCD). Approach and use research methods, conduct studies, then identify, frame, and analyze user needs. Understand forms of User Research Documentation: personas, empathy maps, journey maps... and their role in design. Recognize the importance of technology and business context.
assessments.Grading Guide: Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 3 weeks. Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly. During review sessions, students must present how AI was used, discuss AI-generated issues with the instructor, and justify their design choices before the final presentation. Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.

assessments.No Question: Assignment 2: Experience Design Students will transform insights from assignment 1 into design solutions by proposing appropriate features, then define the information architecture, user flows, develop wireframes, and conduct heuristic usability testing before creating UI and simple interactive prototypes. Students must submit information architecture, user flows, and wireframes via Figma link.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Apply UX principles to transform research insights into design solutions. Understand and structure information architecture, user flows, and wireframes. Recognize the role of usability testing in refining design.
assessments.Grading Guide: Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks. Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly. Students are required to use AI for heuristic usability evaluation. They must document AI feedback, compare it with learned UX principles, and update their design accordingly. Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.No Question: Assignment 3: User Interface & Prototype Design Students will build on insights and outputs from assignments 1 and 2 to design the full user interface and create a high-fidelity interactive prototype of their application. The focus is on applying effective design practices to develop visually appealing, consistent, and functional interfaces that enhance user experience. Students must submit a complete high-fidelity prototype via a shareable link with full, engaging interactions. Submission should also include persuasive promotional materials like poster,showcase portfolio or walkthrought video showcasing the app and its interface.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Students gain the ability to apply design practices to build high-fidelity prototypes Refine UI for clarity and consistency Demonstrate interactive functionality Present the app effectively through persuasive visuals and promotional media.
assessments.Grading Guide: Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks. Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly. Students are required to use AI for heuristic usability evaluation. They must document AI feedback, compare it with learned UX principles, and update their design accordingly. Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.
